summary: Full-extraction pass on the Hungarian Competition Authority (GVH) informant-reward FAQ page and its annual reports to Parliament for 2010 and 2012-2016. The reports give only a few programme numbers a year (enquiries, admitted applications); most were already in the data. Added the 2010 split of enquiries, 2011 enquiries, 2016 proceedings prepared from the reward and Kartell Chat, and the FAQ procedural rules.

Other exclusions in FAQ 5 (evidence obtained by crime or petty offence; no fine imposed, incl. cases taken over by the European Commission; evidence split only to multiply rewards; breach of GVH-ordered cooperation) are described in the ledger contains, not as rows.

new_indicators.name: Proceedings opened on whistleblower information
new_indicators.definition: Investigations or proceedings an authority opened (or prepared to open) in a period on the basis of information from whistleblowers or informants; breakdown item= says which channel or programme.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-whistleblowing-hun1 (GVH 2016 report: 1 proceeding from the informant reward, 2 from Kartell Chat).

gaps: No GVH report in this batch gives reward amounts paid or the number of rewards paid; 2016 gives no informant-enquiry count.

ledger.contains: GVH web page (undated, current at 2026-10-05): 13 questions and answers on the informant reward under Tpvt. s. 79/A. Covers why rewards are paid; what a hardcore cartel is; which evidence qualifies (indispensable written evidence, or information enabling a court-authorised dawn raid that finds such evidence); who may inform (any natural person); exclusions (staff of a prior leniency applicant, evidence obtained by crime or petty offence, evidence split to multiply rewards, no fine imposed incl. cases taken over by the European Commission, breach of GVH-ordered cooperation); criminal-law context (Criminal Code s. 420: 1-5 years for bid-rigging cartels; immunity only for those reporting first to criminal authorities or under a corporate leniency application: out of scope); contact details (Detection Office, anonymous enquiry and Kartell Chat); procedure (anonymous prior enquiry; 5-day deadline to claim after notification; separate order if evidence unsuitable; preliminary assessments not binding); decision within 30 days of the closing decision and payment due 30 days after the order is final; amount 1% of all fines in the case, max HUF 50 million, free of personal income tax; not reclaimable if a court later cuts the fine unless the evidence proves unlawful through the informant's fault; one reward per person per case, separate rewards for separate people; informant may be heard as a witness and can ask for sealed identity data. No statistics. Anonymous filing of a reward claim is not provided (only anonymous enquiries; identity can be sealed), so no anonymous_filing row. Rules extracted: pct min/max, filing deadline, decision and payment deadlines, tax exemption, leniency-staff exclusion (cap already in data).

GVH annual report to Parliament on 2010 (96 pp.): competition enforcement (cartels, abuse of dominance, mergers, consumer protection), fines, court review, advocacy, international work, budget and staff. Programme content only on PDF p. 7 (informant reward introduced 1 April 2010: 1% of fine, max HUF 50 million; about 20 private persons came forward vs 2-3 non-complainant signals a year before; 50% not cartel, 40% cartel but not meeting the law's requirements, 10% application admitted), p. 35 (reward mentioned as a detection tool) and p. 69 (press conference end of March 2010). Rule rows, launch event and tips_received 2010 were already in the data; added the three shares and the press-conference event. The 2-3 pre-reward signals a year are not a programme number (before launch) and are left out. Everything else (cartel fines e.g. HUF 9.6 bn in 2010, leniency applications 3) is out of scope.

GVH annual report to Parliament on 2012 (126 pp.): enforcement, fines, consumer protection, advocacy, budget. Programme content: PDF p. 9 (nearly 20 informant inquiries in 2012 as in 2011; most did not meet the legal requirements; no details on admitted applications), p. 46 (number of enquiries about the reward unchanged from 2011 but applications actually filed fell, possibly from fear of losing anonymity: words only, no numbers) and p. 47 (informants mentioned alongside an OLAF referral). Added tips_received 2011 (the 2012 row was already in the data). Cartel fines (HUF 1,250 million in 2012), leniency (3 applications) and other activity are out of scope.

GVH annual report to Parliament on 2013 (148 pp.). Programme content: PDF p. 10 (2013 talks with about 25-30 potential applicants, one application admitted; first proceeding opened largely on an informant's information closed in 2013, Vj-43/2011 office supplies, eleven companies fined HUF 1,003.6 million, reward payable over HUF 10 million; others failed the indispensability test or withdrew from fear) and p. 53 (office-supplies cartel decided in December 2013; no further reward numbers); p. 7, 16, 19-20, 25 on the new Detection Office (set up 15 April 2013) without reward numbers; p. 101 decision table lists Vj-43/2011 with the HUF 1,003,600,000 fine. All in-scope rows (tips 25-30, 1 admitted, the case) were already in the data; nothing new to add. Rest of the report (other cases, fines, leniency, consumer protection, budget) out of scope.

GVH annual report to Parliament on 2014 (122 pp.). Programme content: PDF p. 13 (informant enquiries rose again in 2014 after the 2013 dip; about 20 potential informant enquiries, 2 applications admitted; informant reward said to help detection more than leniency, of which none admitted in 2014) and p. 22 (calendar: 24 January 2014 press conference on the first cartel case with an informant reward payment). All three items were already in the data; nothing new. Rest (fines, other cases, consumer protection, budget) out of scope.

GVH annual report to Parliament on 2015 (160 pp.). Programme content: PDF p. 15 (informant-reward enquiries unchanged from the previous year at 20; no new informant application admitted in 2015 because none met the legal conditions), p. 16 (informant reward and leniency both fluctuate), p. 10, 21, 26, 29, 103-104 (Kartell Chat anonymous contact channel introduced in 2015, press conference 25 November 2015, Honorable Mention award). tips_received 2015 and admitted 0 were already in the data; added the Kartell Chat launch as a context event. Leniency (3 admitted), fines and the rest are out of scope.

GVH annual report to Parliament on 2016 (158 pp.). Programme content: PDF p. 5 and 8 (Kartell Chat a new information source alongside leniency and the informant reward), p. 12 (20 Kartell Chat contacts matched the average number of informant-reward enquiries; 2 proceedings prepared from Kartell Chat, 1 from the informant reward; leniency applications admitted 2), p. 100 (Kartell Chat in operation since December 2015; 20 registered in 2016; Honorable Mention April 2016) and p. 146 (GVH comment on the budget law asking for exceptions for informant-reward payments from the centralised fine account; 2016 Act CXLII: words only). No count of informant-reward enquiries, applications or payments for 2016 is printed. Added proceedings from the reward (1) and Kartell Chat (2) under a proposed indicator, and Kartell Chat registrations (20). Image charts (fines by year) are about general enforcement; out of scope.
